Trapp's perspective seeks to elevate Virgil’s work, positioning it alongside that of Homer and others. He aims to establish a framework for understanding Virgil's work, arguing that its beauty lies not only in its narrative but also in the emotional resonance it elicits from the reader, affirming its place within the canon of great literary works.
